classification.reason: Request is a scientific goal or asks for planning without a concrete workflow.

plan.goal: Generate one small soluble de novo protein candidate with ESM3, perform sequence-level and structural QC, annotate secondary structure with DSSP, and produce a deterministically ranked output.
assumptions: A 60-residue seed sequence (20-aa alphabet repeated 3×) is used as the de novo starting point; no target length was specified, so 60 residues is a reasonable small-soluble default (40–80 aa range).
Fold class and topology are unconstrained; ESM3 samples from its learned distribution over the seed.
Temperature 0.7 is chosen to encourage moderate sequence diversity while keeping generation stable for a single-candidate run.
No functional-site, hotspot, or binding constraints are applied; the workflow is purely de novo.
Solubility is assessed indirectly from sequence_analysis charge/composition liabilities and structure_analysis RSA-based exposure metrics.
rank_designs is called with top_k=1 because exactly one candidate is produced; ranking still provides a normalised score record.
DSSP is run as an explicit upstream node so its per-residue annotation record is available as a discrete QC artefact for rank_designs, even though structure_analysis also runs DSSP internally.

success_criteria.candidate_generated: ESM3 emits a valid amino-acid sequence and a PDB structure file for the de novo candidate
success_criteria.sequence_qc_complete: sequence_analysis returns composition, charge at pH 7.4, region annotations, and flagged liabilities with no fatal errors
success_criteria.secondary_structure_annotated: dssp assigns H/E/C labels to every residue of the ESM3 PDB
success_criteria.structural_qc_complete: structure_analysis returns per-residue RSA, contacts, and exposure summary without parser errors
success_criteria.ranked_output_produced: rank_designs returns a top-1 ranked candidate record aggregating all upstream metrics
